pis.name: Prof. Marco Rasponi
pis.bio: Full Professor of Bioengineering with expertise in microfluidics and organ-on-chip systems. Leading research in biomimetic devices and tissue engineering.
pis.bioFull:
Professor Marco Rasponi is the founder and director of the MiMic Lab at DEIB, Politecnico di Milano. His research focuses on developing advanced microfluidic platforms for drug discovery and disease modeling. With over 80 publications in peer-reviewed journals and numerous patents, he has established himself as a leading expert in organ-on-chip technology.

Prof. Rasponi received his PhD from Politecnico di Milano and has received several prestigious awards. His lab collaborates with leading pharmaceutical companies and academic institutions worldwide.

pis.name: Prof. Paola Occhetta
pis.bio: Associate Professor specializing in mechanobiology and cartilage-on-chip systems. Expert in 3D tissue models and mechanical stimulation platforms.
pis.bioFull:
Professor Paola Occhetta is Associate Professor at DEIB, Politecnico di Milano, where she leads research on mechanobiology and osteoarthritis modeling using organ-on-chip technology. Her work focuses on understanding how mechanical forces influence tissue development and disease progression.

Prof. Occhetta has published extensively in the field of cartilage engineering and microfluidic systems. She collaborates with orthopedic researchers and pharmaceutical companies to develop predictive models for joint diseases.

members.name: Dr. Maria Bianchi
members.bio: Research focus: microfluidic device fabrication and characterization for cardiac tissue modeling.
members.bioFull: Dr. Maria Bianchi joined the lab in 2022 after completing her PhD at University of Cambridge. Her research focuses on developing heart MiMic systems with integrated biosensors for real-time monitoring of cardiac function. She has published 15 papers in high-impact journals and has been awarded the Marie Curie Fellowship.

members.name: Dr. Luca Verdi
members.bio: Expertise in biosensor integration and electrochemical detection in microfluidic systems.
members.bioFull: Dr. Luca Verdi specializes in integrating advanced biosensors into MiMic platforms. With a background in electrical engineering and bioelectronics, he develops novel sensing strategies for metabolite detection and tissue monitoring.

members.name: Sofia Romano
members.bio: Working on liver MiMic models for drug toxicity testing and metabolism studies.
members.bioFull: Sofia is a third-year PhD student developing liver MiMic platforms with hepatocyte co-cultures. Her work aims to create predictive models for drug-induced liver injury.

members.name: Alessandro Ferrari
members.bio: Developing gut MiMic systems with integrated microbiome for studying host-microbe interactions.
members.bioFull: Alessandro's research combines microfluidics with microbiology to create gut models that incorporate the intestinal microbiome. His work has implications for understanding inflammatory bowel diseases.

members.name: Giulia Conti
members.bio: Focus on 3D bioprinting and biomaterials for creating vascularized tissue constructs.
members.bioFull: Giulia combines 3D bioprinting with MiMic technology to create vascularized tissues. Her interdisciplinary approach bridges materials science and tissue engineering.

members.name: Matteo Esposito
members.bio: Developing lung MiMic models for studying respiratory diseases and air-liquid interface cultures.
members.bioFull: Matteo's research focuses on creating physiologically relevant lung models that replicate breathing mechanics and air exposure. His work contributes to understanding respiratory infections and pollution effects.

members.name: Elena Marino
members.bio: Thesis project on microfluidic gradient generators for chemotaxis studies.

members.name: Francesco Ricci
members.bio: Working on automated image analysis pipelines for MiMic experiments.
